subject: English
passage: The composer Elena Petrov made significant contributions to the development of early twentieth-century Russian classical music, but her work has remained largely unknown in Western Europe except among musicologists. One reason for Petrov's relative obscurity is the enormous fame of some of her contemporaries. In particular, the composers Igor Stravinsky and Sergei Rachmaninoff have so dominated the attention of European audiences that Petrov and other Russian composers from the period often go unrecognized, despite the exceptional quality of their compositions.
prompt: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

choices.A: Petrov's work is not as well-known in Western Europe as it should be because Stravinsky and Rachmaninoff draw so much of the public's attention.
choices.B: During Petrov's lifetime, her compositions were performed in European concert halls much more frequently than works by Stravinsky and Rachmaninoff were.
choices.C: Petrov composed music in some of the same styles that Stravinsky and Rachmaninoff used but employed different harmonic structures than they employed.
choices.D: Few of Petrov's compositions are performed today because she wrote only a small number of works.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because it most accurately states the main idea of the text. The text explains that Petrov made significant contributions to Russian classical music but lacks recognition in Western Europe because Stravinsky and Rachmaninoff dominate public attention.
